baseline_size_requirement.interpretation: At the pilot baseline (m=30) the median in-control ARL0 stays near the nominal 370 but the 5th-percentile (unlucky-baseline) ARL0 is far lower and P(ARL0<200) is non-negligible: the <=5% false-alarm budget holds in EXPECTATION (median 30-batch expected false alarms << 1.5) but NOT with high assurance for any single realized baseline. Recovering guaranteed near-nominal performance needs a substantially larger baseline, consistent with Quesenberry's m>=300 recommendation for Individuals charts.

closes: Quantifies, for the first time in this module, the estimated-parameter (finite baseline) degradation of the Shewhart Individuals in-control ARL0 -- the explicit Phase-1 gap left open by spc-arl-characterization-v1.

Reproduces control-chart constants c4(n) and d2(n=2) vs Montgomery/NIST tables (max abs err < 5e-4) and recovers the known-parameter ARL0=370.40 as the m->inf limit, cross-anchoring the prior receipt.
Deterministic 2-D quadrature of the conditional ARL0 law is independently corroborated by pinned-seed Monte-Carlo integration (percentile agreement < 3%).

Turns the module's locked <=5% false-alarm KPI into a concrete baseline-size requirement: budget holds in expectation at m=30 but guaranteed performance needs a much larger baseline (Quesenberry m>=300).
does_not_close: Does NOT establish real-batch acceptability, product qualification, EHS acceptability, or batch-release authority.

Covers only the Shewhart Individuals chart with the sample-S sigma estimator; the moving-range estimator (MR-bar/d2) has fewer effective degrees of freedom so degrades at least as much (conservative direction), and estimated-parameter EWMA (Jones 2002) / CUSUM guaranteed-ARL remain open.
Assumes i.i.d. normal in-control data; non-normality and autocorrelation are not modeled.
No prospective time-ordered 30-batch pilot is checked in; this is a theory characterization, not a recall/false-alarm measurement on real batches.

c4_constant_known_answer.source: Montgomery ISQC 8e Appendix VI; NIST e-Handbook 6.3.2

d2_constant_known_answer.source: Montgomery ISQC Appendix VI (n=2); NIST e-Handbook 6.3.2

known_parameter_limit_m_to_inf.note: As baseline m->inf the estimated-parameter ARL0 law collapses to the known-parameter geometric point mass ARL0=370.40 (self-consistency vs spc-arl-characterization-v1). The MEDIAN converges fast (rel err ~3e-5 at m=1e6); the 5th-percentile converges only as O(m^-1/2) because sd(S/sigma) ~ 1/sqrt(2m) and dARL/dW is steep near L=3 sigma -- i.e. guaranteed low-percentile performance needs a very large baseline, the quantitative content of the Quesenberry-1993 m>=300 rule itself.

mc_quadrature_method_agreement.note: Independent pinned-seed Monte-Carlo integration corroborates the deterministic quadrature percentiles (tail-insensitive summaries).

headline: Estimated-parameter ARL0 degradation for the module's Shewhart Individuals chart (L=3), computed exactly over the joint sampling law of (Xbar,S) and cross-checked by pinned-seed Monte Carlo. At the module's m=20-30 pilot baseline the in-control run-length law is right-skewed and the GUARANTEED (5th-pct) ARL0 collapses far below the nominal 370.4, quantifying the Quesenberry-1993 finite-baseline penalty the prior known-parameter receipt flagged as a best-case bound.

kpi_linkage.closes_prior_does_not_close_item: spc-arl-characterization-v1 does_not_close: 'the module estimates limits from a finite baseline, so real ARL0 is shorter and right-skewed (Quesenberry 1993) -- known-parameter figures are a BEST-CASE bound.'
kpi_linkage.module_locked_kpi: prospective 30-batch pilot: seeded-control recall >=90%, false alarms <=5%, zero false releases

non_circularity: Uses only closed-form / exactly-quadratured sampling distributions of the Shewhart estimators (Xbar ~ N, (m-1)S^2/sigma^2 ~ chi^2_{m-1}) and published control-chart constants (c4,d2). Independent of the module's self-authored synthetic universes, of the arithmetic-correctness KPI receipt, and of the known-parameter ARL tables in spc-arl-characterization-v1 (which it instead recovers as the m->inf limit).
purpose: Convert the qualitative 'real ARL0 is shorter and right-skewed (Quesenberry 1993)' caveat of spc-arl-characterization-v1 into a quantified, signed baseline-size requirement for the module's locked <=5% false-alarm KPI.

theory_reference.chart_constants: Montgomery Introduction to SQC 8th ed. Appendix VI; NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook 6.3.2 (c4, d2).
theory_reference.estimated_parameter_arl: Quesenberry 1993 J.Qual.Technol. 25(4):237-247 (SPC Q-charts / m>=300 rule for Individuals); Jensen, Jones-Farmer, Champ, Woodall 2006 J.Qual.Technol. 38(4):349-364 (review); Saleh, Mahmoud, Keefe, Woodall 2015 J.Qual.Technol. 47(2):127-138 (conditional/guaranteed perf).
